headline: Tishomingo County School Board Meeting for May
summary: The board approved personnel, field trips, fundraisers, donations and purchases including a three-year math curriculum, MSWIN bus radios and a Burnsville concession stand, and adopted a resolution declaring its intent to borrow up to $3,500,000 in notes for capital improvements and buses. It also approved pay scale increases for principals and assistant principals, added two K-8 instructional coach positions and revised the staff-student non-fraternization policy.

personnel.note: Hires include 10 summer workers at $10/hour, 2 substitute bus drivers, a cafeteria substitute and several coaching and bus-route assignments (people listed twice counted once); other = 3 license upgrades, 2 contract corrections and 2 volunteers.

Cast aluminum architectural prismatic letters for a district sports complex (lowest quote)
IEP and Section 504 plan management software, 3 years (2025/26-2027/28), lowest quote
Resolution declaring intent to borrow money and issue notes for capital improvements and purchase of buses
Pay scale increase for assistant principals
K-8 math and K-8 ELA instructional coach positions (teacher pay scale plus supplement), 2025/26
MSWIN bus radios, Mississippi State Contract 21276
Tree removal around TCHS to allow for lights
Construction of Burnsville football/baseball concession stand (lowest quote)

policy.item: Revised the GABB policy on staff-student non-fraternization.

superintendent: Superintendent Christie Holly reported that the company replacing the doors and press boxes is waiting for testing at the campuses to be completed before preparing the bid.
Dropout figures were reported: four students at TCHS (one left to be home schooled) and 17 at Belmont School (eight left to be home schooled).
